title: SDK Playbook: Tool Simulator + Interactive Replay (PRD sketch)
body:
Context and problem statement:

We keep hearing from SDK users and internal solutions engineers: it is hard to develop and test tool-integrated flows that rely on partial/streaming output. Two main developer pain points keep repeating:

1) No easy local way to run an approximation of hosted behavior for rapid iteration. Developers either mock tool responses crudely or run against staging which is slow and noisy.
2) Reproducing production errors that are tied to timing (partial frames, mid-stream tool handshakes, retries, hedging) is painful — replay is fragile because of nondeterministic model outputs and live tool latencies.

Goal (high level):
- Provide a lightweight SDK playbook and small runtime components that let developers: (a) simulate tool backends deterministically, (b) record and replay streaming sessions (with configurable fuzzing), and (c) test structured output and tool-call ergonomics locally/offline.
- Reduce bug->fix cycle for streaming+tool-call UX by 3x for internal devs and external integrators.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- UX/ergonomics for SDK integration points: how to plug simulators and recorders into app code with minimal changes
- Design sketches for a small "tool-simulator" microservice and a lightweight "session-recorder" that can run locally or as a CI job
- Replay semantics for partial/streamed frames, function/tool calls, and structured JSON/iterative outputs
- Telemetry and assertions to help detect divergence between live and simulated runs

Out of scope (for this iteration):
- Full end-to-end integration with Redwood Dedicated or Private backplanes (we do basic compatibility testing but not deployment automation)
- Formal SDK API freeze; this is a playbook + prototype rather than final surface spec

Use cases and user journeys (short):
- Developer iterates on a multi-step toolflow: runs locally with tool-simulator that returns canned responses and controlled latencies; can flip between deterministic-mode and fuzz-mode to test edge cases.
- QA/SE runs a recorded session from production through the session-recorder, replays into staging with injected delays to validate graceful degradation.
- Customer solutions engineer shares a replay bundle (session trace + tooling config) with product/eng to reproduce a customer's bug without exposing PII (supports scrub rules).

Key requirements (developer-centered):
- Low-friction: integrate by changing 1 line of config or by swapping a small SDK helper object in DI/container
- Deterministic default: recording captures model outputs, token-level frames, tool call boundaries, and tool responses; replays default to exact sequence
- Configurable fuzzing: replay can inject latency, drop frames, mutate tool responses, or change tokenization boundaries to simulate real-world noise
- Privacy-aware: replay bundles must support scrub/replace rules to remove PII before sharing
- Streaming-first: must model partial frames, incremental JSON patches, and chunked tool-handshakes, not only final messages

Design sketches

1) Components (lightweight):
- sdk-recorder (client-side lib): intercepts SDK calls (stream start, frame events, tool call initiation/complete), writes a compact trace (NDJSON) with timestamped events and optional compressed token payloads.
- tool-simulator (dev microservice): takes a trace or a small behavior script and exposes a simple HTTP/WS endpoint that mimics tool behavior (delays, error codes, chunking). Supports content templates and parameterized responses.
- replay-driver (CLI): consumes a trace, runs through replay rules, and proxies traffic to the app or to a test endpoint. Has modes: exact, fuzz-latency, mutate-output, drop-frames.

2) Trace format (brief):
- NDJSON, each line a flat object: event_type, ts_iso, session_id, token_chunk_base64 (optional), tool_call_id (optional), tool_response_base64 (optional), meta_tags (list).
- Keep format intentionally simple to avoid nested JSON in traces (easier to stream/process).

3) SDK ergonomics / API suggestions (pseudo):
- session = Redwood.session({recorder: new Recorder({enabled: true, redact: redactRules})})
- session.stream(prompt, {onToken: (tok)=>{}, onPartialJSON: (doc)=>{}, onToolCall: (call)=>{ /* app can decide to allow/deny */ }})
- localSimulator = new ToolSimulator('sim-config.json')
- session.setToolEndpoint('search', localSimulator.endpoint)
- CLI: redwood-replay play --trace my.trace.ndjson --mode fuzz-latency --seed 42

Developer ergonomics notes:
- Make recorder an opt-in switch; default off for privacy. Enable through env var REDWOOD_RECORDER=1 or SDK flag to make it easy in dev but safe in prod.
- Provide a single line shim to swap endpoints: redwood.setToolRouter(localSimulator.router) so tests don't rewire call-sites.
- Provide helpers to create small fixture traces (e.g., from a JSON story) so unit tests can include stable replay assets in repo.

Replay semantics and nondeterminism handling:
- Exact mode: feed recorded token chunks and tool responses back verbatim. Good for deterministic regression tests.
- Tolerant mode: keep tool-call boundaries, but allow model token variance. Replayer will attempt to align by token heuristics (prefix match) and if misaligned, emit an alignment event.
- Fuzz mode: inject delays, drop or duplicate frames, or swap tool responses to validate error paths.
- Checkpointing: insert named checkpoints in traces so replays can resume from mid-session; helpful for long workflows.

Observability and assertions built into playbook:
- Replay-run generates a diff log (frame-by-frame) and summary: alignment score, tool-call match rate, frames-dropped, timeouts injected.
- SDK exposes assertion hooks: expectNoPartialJSONErrors(), expectToolCallOrder(['search','dbRead']). These are simple JS helpers for tests.

Security and privacy considerations:
- Redaction rules applied at recorder: regex for emails, api-keys, credit-card-like patterns. Provide CLI scrubbing step: redwood-replay scrub --in raw.trace --out scrubbed.trace --rules default-scrub.json
- Access control: replay bundles should be small files and treated as artifacts; for sharing we recommend packager that strips or masks user IDs and uploads to an internal blobstore with short-lived links.

Proposed rollout plan (MVP -> Beta -> Opt-in GA):
- MVP (4 weeks): sdk-recorder basic NDJSON trace + local tool-simulator with canned responses + replay-driver exact mode + CLI to play trace locally. Internal-only.
- Beta (8 weeks): add fuzz modes, CLI scrubber, test helpers in SDK, CI integration example, initial docs and examples. Invite 5 internal teams.
- Opt-in GA (quarter): polish ergonomics, add replay UI in Console (upload/inspect trace), provide hosted sandbox for replaying trimmed traces (privacy-safe), add support for replaying against Dedicated staging.

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Trace size: token-level captures could be large. Compression and selective capture strategies (token sampling) needed. Decide default (capture first N tokens per request?).
- Telemetry: what events do we ship back to product telemetry (only counts/metrics, not traces) to measure adoption?
- Language SDK parity: prioritize JS/TS + Python initially; later go to Go and Java SDKs.
- How to represent streaming partial JSON patches in the trace cleanly without nested objects? Proposal: base64-encoded chunk payload plus a mime-type tag.

Next steps (owners):
- Prototype recorder and CLI (Asha, Devon) — spike: 2 weeks
- Prototype tool-simulator (Luis) — 2 weeks parallel
- Internal playtest with support-engineering (Mei) — schedule week 3
- Scrub rules matrix and legal review (Ravi + Security) — week 4

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Could reuse existing streaming wire protocol code in SDK to hook recorder with minimal duplication.
- Consider small electron-based GUI for constructing jitter/fuzz scenarios visually (later).
- If this proves valuable, a hosted "replay sandbox" could be a differentiator for enterprise debugging without exposing raw PII.

References and existing artifacts:
- GH PR with preliminary tracer: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/1243
- Internal convo: slack #hosted-api ts:1678437620.000300
- Ticket: JIRA API-8421 (replay/recorder epic)

End of sketch.
